definitions.explanation: a situation where no progress can be made; a point where further action becomes impossible

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}は{行|い}き{詰|づ}まりに{達|たっ}した。
{経営|けいえい}の{行|い}き{詰|づ}まりで{倒産|とうさん}した。
examples.english: The company went bankrupt due to a management impasse.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{詰|づ}まりを{打開|だかい}する{方法|ほうほう}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: We are looking for a way to break the deadlock.

notes:
VERB FORM:
{行|い}き{詰|づ}まる (to reach an impasse, to be deadlocked)

USAGE:
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まりに{達|たっ}する (to reach a deadlock)
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まりを{感|かん}じる (to feel stuck)
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まりを{打開|だかい}する (to break the deadlock)

CONTEXT:
Used in business, politics, negotiations, and personal situations when a situation has become stuck and needs intervention to move forward.
